messages.subject: predicting intensity in a 2d spde + covariates
parts:
Hello all,

I am having some trouble interpreting the help and tutorials regarding predictions from spatial models that include covariates. After generating a set of points for the prediction and the corresponding A matrix, when I try to stack them I get the error  

Error in (function (data, A, effects, tag = "", compress = TRUE, remove.unused = TRUE)  : 
  Row count mismatch for A: 109816,4658

I am pretty sure there's something obvious I'm missing but I've read those tutorials from front to back and back to front again and still can't quite make sense of it. Any help will be greatly appreciated. 

Code follows, and is also attached together with the data: 

library("INLA")
load("inla_pred_fail.Rdata")

# funtion to generate dual mesh (??)
inla.mesh.dual <- function(mesh) {
  if (mesh$manifold=='R2') {
    ce <- t(sapply(1:nrow(mesh$graph$tv), function(i)
      colMeans(mesh$loc[mesh$graph$tv[i, ], 1:2])))
    library(parallel)
    pls <- mclapply(1:mesh$n, function(i) {
      p <- unique(Reduce('rbind', lapply(1:3, function(k) {
        j <- which(mesh$graph$tv[,k]==i)
        if (length(j)>0) 
          return(rbind(ce[j, , drop=FALSE],
                       cbind(mesh$loc[mesh$graph$tv[j, k], 1] +
                               mesh$loc[mesh$graph$tv[j, c(2:3,1)[k]], 1], 
                             mesh$loc[mesh$graph$tv[j, k], 2] +
                               mesh$loc[mesh$graph$tv[j, c(2:3,1)[k]], 2])/2))
        else return(ce[j, , drop=FALSE])
      })))
      j1 <- which(mesh$segm$bnd$idx[,1]==i)
      j2 <- which(mesh$segm$bnd$idx[,2]==i)
      if ((length(j1)>0) | (length(j2)>0)) {
        p <- unique(rbind(mesh$loc[i, 1:2], p,
                          mesh$loc[mesh$segm$bnd$idx[j1, 1], 1:2]/2 +
                            mesh$loc[mesh$segm$bnd$idx[j1, 2], 1:2]/2, 
                          mesh$loc[mesh$segm$bnd$idx[j2, 1], 1:2]/2 +
                            mesh$loc[mesh$segm$bnd$idx[j2, 2], 1:2]/2))
        yy <- p[,2]-mean(p[,2])/2-mesh$loc[i, 2]/2
        xx <- p[,1]-mean(p[,1])/2-mesh$loc[i, 1]/2
      }
      else {
        yy <- p[,2]-mesh$loc[i, 2]
        xx <- p[,1]-mesh$loc[i, 1]
      }
      Polygon(p[order(atan2(yy,xx)), ])
    })
    return(SpatialPolygons(lapply(1:mesh$n, function(i)
      Polygons(list(pls[[i]]), i))))
  }
  else stop("It only works for R2!")
}

#create spde model
spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh=mesh, alpha=2,### mesh and smoothness parameter
                            prior.range=c(300, 0.01), ### P(practic.range<300)=0.01
                            prior.sigma=c(1, 0.1)) ### P(sigma>3)=0.1



# create projector matrix and response variabla
sum(diag(spde$param.inla$M0))
dmesh <- inla.mesh.dual(mesh)
par(mfrow=c(1,2));plot(mesh);plot(dmesh)

# number of meshnodes and number of datapoints
(nv <- mesh$n)
(n <- nrow(ds.df3))


# calculate weights for each meshnode depending on whether they are inside or outside the boundary
sum(w <- sapply(1:length(dmesh), function(i) {
  if (gIntersects(dmesh[i,], bound))
    return(gArea(gIntersection(dmesh[i,], bound)))
  else return(0)
}))

table(w>0)

# plot mesh, weights, and boundary. As we are working with lgcp we don't mind the integration points being in the nodes of the mesh
par(mar=c(2,2,1,1), mgp=2:0)
plot(mesh$loc, asp=1, col=(w==0)+1, pch=19, xlab='', ylab='')
plot(mesh, add=TRUE)
plot(bound, border=3, add = T)

#response (0 for all meshnodes, 1 for all data points)
length(y.pp <- rep(0:1, c(nv, n)))

# expected (weights at each mesh node and 0 for all data points)
length(e.pp <- c(w, rep(0, n)))

#projector matrix 
lmat <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, ds.df3@coords)
imat <- Diagonal(nv, rep(1, nv))
A.pp <- rBind(imat, lmat)

# make a stack with data, A = observation matrix (projector matrix), effects = predictors (as many as obs matrices)
stk.pp <- inla.stack(data=list(y=y.pp, e=e.pp),
                     A=list(1,A.pp), tag='pp',
                     effects=list(list(Intercept=rep(1,nv+n)), # predictors with the first projector matrix (1)
                                  list(rdm=1:nv))) # predictors with the second projector matrix


## collect covariate at points and mesh nodes

# meshnodes
mshpts2D <- SpatialPoints(coords = cbind(mesh$loc[,1], mesh$loc[,2]))

covariate <- c(extract(bati, mshpts2D), extract(bati, ds.df3))

# the mesh, projector matrix, etc, we recicle from the null mode
stk.cov <- inla.stack(data=list(y=y.pp, e=e.pp),
                      A=list(A.pp, 1), tag='cov',
                      effects=list(list(spat_field = 1:spde$n.spde),
                                   data.frame(Intercept = 1,
                                              gBati = inla.group(covariate))))

# FOR PREDICTION

# generate prediction locations

# dimensions of the lattice
stepsize <- 10
(nxy <- round(c(diff(bound@bbox[1,]),
                diff(bound@bbox[2,])/stepsize)))


# create the projector matrix (just to extract the lattice points)
projgrid <- inla.mesh.projector(mesh, xlim=bound@bbox[1,], ylim=bound@bbox[2,], dims=nxy)
predpts <- SpatialPoints(projgrid$lattice$loc, bbox = bound@bbox)

# extract bati value at each prediction point
batipred <- extract(raster_list[[1]],predpts)


# create projector matrix with prediction points
dim(A.pred <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc=predpts)) #as many rows as datapoints, as many columns as meshpoints

# create the stack for the prediction (data = NA)
stk.prd <- inla.stack(data=list(y = NA),
                      tag = "pred_bati",
                      A=list(A.pred, 1),
                      effects=list(list(spat_field = 1:spde$n.spde),
                                   data.frame(Intercept = 1,
                                              gBati = inla.group(covariate))))

Alrighty, sorry about the lack of detail before, here it goes a bit more worked out:

The raster file for the covariate that seems to be missing can be found here, but really, any values will do for now, it's just to test what I'm doing wrong with the stack.

First of all, the first half of the (updated) script is just setting up the stack for fitting the model, following instructions from the SPDE tutorial in the website. The only difference is that I get the values for the covariates extracting from a raster file (the one that was missing, that is attached now). I am not going to break it down here because it's basically the same code from the tutorial.

Then, when I get on to try and prepare a stack for the prediction, is when I find problems. So, from line 125 of the script, onwards:

#To set the dimensions of the lattice into which to predict:

stepsize <- 10
(nxy <- round(c(diff(bound@bbox[1,]),
                diff(bound@bbox[2,])/stepsize)))

This gives me a vector with two elements

> 742 148

Then, to generate a set of points on regular locations all over my study area, I use:

# create the projector matrix (just to extract the lattice points)
projgrid <- inla.mesh.projector(mesh, xlim=bound@bbox[1,], ylim=bound@bbox[2,], dims=nxy)
predpts <- SpatialPoints(projgrid$lattice$loc, bbox = bound@bbox)

(sure there are better ways than inla.mesh.projector for that, but this was just handy)

now predpts is a SpatialPoints dataframe: 

class       : SpatialPoints 
features    : 109816 
extent      : 6561.982, 7304.386, 820.2731, 2296.467  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
coord. ref. : NA 

Here, I extract the values from the raster on my prediction points: 

batipred <- extract(bati,predpts)


And now batipred is a vector with values for my covariate at all the prediction points

> length(batipred)
[1] 109816

I create a projector matrix with the same mesh as before but the new predpoints as argument "loc"

# create projector matrix with prediction points

> dim(A.pred <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc=predpts)) #as many rows as datapoints, as many columns as meshpoints

[1] 109816    564


Finally, with this projector matrix, I try and create a new stack for prediction and that's when I get the error:
> stk.prd <- inla.stack(data=list(y = NA),

+                       tag = "pred_bati",
+                       A=list(A.pred, 1),
+                       effects=list(list(spat_field = 1:spde$n.spde),
+                                    data.frame(Intercept = 1,
+                                               gBati = inla.group(covariate))))

Error in (function (data, A, effects, tag = "", compress = TRUE, remove.unused = TRUE)  : 
  Row count mismatch for A: 109816,4658

Thanks again for any help!

BEECA
University of Barcelona

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] predicting intensity in a 2d spde + covariates
parts:
I set bati@file@name <- "bathymetry.tif" to be able to run the code,
changed raster_list[[1]] to bati when creating batipred, and the
problem is that you're not using the extracted batipred values for the
prediction stack.
You need

stk.prd <- inla.stack(data=list(y = NA),
tag = "pred_bati",
A=list(A.pred, 1),
effects=list(list(spat_field = 1:spde$n.spde),
data.frame(Intercept = 1,

gBati = inla.group(batipred))))

but you had inla.group(covariate) there.

Note: You don't really use it, but there's an error in the tutorial
document for obtaining the mesh area:
sum(diag(spde$param.inla$M0))
is not guaranteed to be the right thing. Use
sum(inla.mesh.fem(mesh)$va)
instead.

Finn
